raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On PCIe-only boxes, `CustomAllReduceV2` requires full NVLink, so sglang falls back to the legacy v1 `CustomAllreduce`. When `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` is set (the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook recommends it for long contexts), CUDA-graph inputs come from `cuMemCreate` memory. During capture v1 records those pointers, and `register_graph_buffers` -> `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta` calls `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` on them, which only accepts `cudaMalloc` memory. The server dies during graph capture with `RuntimeError: invalid argument`. This is attempt 1 in #44291.

Reproduced on 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, PCIe, no NVLink, P2P OK), `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` at a6a8c5601, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--tp-size 2`:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| default allocator | boots, v1 registers 2850 + 2052 graph addresses |
| `expandable_segments:True` | `RuntimeError: invalid argument` in `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta` |
| `expandable_segments:True` + `SGLANG_ENABLE_PCIE_IPC_ALLREDUCE=1` | same failure; v1 still captures alongside PCIe-IPC |
| `expandable_segments:True` + this PR | boots, same output as the default run at temperature 0 |

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py`: during capture, an input that is VMM memory (checked with the existing `is_vmm_pointer`) goes through the staged path, which copies it into v1's pre-registered `cudaMalloc` IPC buffer. That is the path `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH` already uses, so no kernel or sgl-kernel change is needed. Non-VMM inputs keep the registered path exactly as before. The check is per input, so it also covers the memory saver and symmetric-memory pools, and it only runs at capture time.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce_v1_vmm.py`: new 2-GPU test that runs v1 under `expandable_segments`, captures 4 all-reduces per graph (inputs from a plain tensor and from the graph's own pool), and compares against NCCL exactly.

Why not zero-copy like v2's `VmmGraphInputManager`: v1's graph slots only take `cudaIpc` handles, so zero-copy would need a new AOT op and an sgl-kernel release. Staging reuses a path that is already in production.

## Accuracy Tests

- New test on the PCIe pod: without this PR `1 failed, 1 passed` (`test_graph_all_reduce_matches_nccl[16-False]` raises `RuntimeError: invalid argument`); with it `9 passed`.
- Server: with `expandable_segments` + this PR, the smoke request returns the same text as the default allocator at temperature 0.
- Default path with this PR (registered inputs, default allocator): exact match to NCCL at every size from 2 KB to 8 MB.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Decode with `sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, TP2, input 256, output 128, steady-state tok/s:

| Batch | main, default allocator | this PR, default allocator | this PR, `expandable_segments` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 704 | 705 | 681 |
| 8 | 3988 | 3995 | 3883 |
| 32 | 12261 | 12310 | 12030 |

Default users see no change. `expandable_segments` users go from a crash at startup to 2-3% below the default allocator.

Per all-reduce, 8 captured per graph, median of 2 runs:

| Size | v1 registered (default allocator) | v1 staged (`expandable_segments`) | pynccl |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 4.58 us | 5.38 us | 12.39 us |
| 16 KB | 5.25 us | 6.13 us | 14.39 us |
| 1 MB | 42.0 us | 43.1 us | 47.7 us |

Staging adds about 0.8 us at decode sizes and stays 2.3-2.7x faster than falling back to pynccl.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (ruff 0.15.1 format/check, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, the pinned versions)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Refs #44291

@@ -29,6 +29,7 @@
     is_musa,
     log_info_on_rank0,
 )
+from sglang.srt.utils.cuda_vmm_utils import is_vmm_pointer
 
 _is_cuda = is_cuda()
 _is_hip = is_hip()
@@ -37,6 +38,13 @@
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
 
+def _is_vmm_input(inp: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    # cudaIpcGetMemHandle only exports cudaMalloc memory, so a graph input from
+    # cuMemCreate (expandable_segments, the memory saver, symmetric-memory
+    # pools) cannot be registered for IPC and has to be staged instead.
+    return _is_cuda and is_vmm_pointer(inp.data_ptr())
+
+
 class CustomAllreduce:
     _SUPPORTED_WORLD_SIZES = [2, 4, 6, 8]
     _MAX_CAR_SIZE = 8192 * 1024
@@ -313,7 +321,8 @@ def custom_all_reduce(self, input: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
             return None
         if self._IS_CAPTURING:
             if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
-                return self._all_reduce_impl(input, registered=not self.tms_cudagraph)
+                registered = not (self.tms_cudagraph or _is_vmm_input(input))
+                return self._all_reduce_impl(input, registered=registered)
             else:
                 # Could be warmup OR piecewise cuda graph split op execution.
                 # In piecewise cuda graph, split ops run eagerly outside the graph

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+"""CustomAllreduce (v1) CUDA-graph capture when graph inputs are VMM memory.
+
+With expandable_segments, CUDA-graph inputs come from cuMemCreate memory and
+cudaIpcGetMemHandle rejects them when v1 registers graph buffers
+(sglang#44291). v1 must stage such inputs through its pre-registered IPC
+buffer instead.
+
+Usage::
+
+    python test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce_v1_vmm.py
+"""
+
+import os
+
+# PyTorch reads these at the first CUDA allocation, so they have to be set
+# before anything touches the GPU. Newer torch prefers PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF.
+os.environ["PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF"] = "expandable_segments:True"
+os.environ["PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF"] = "expandable_segments:True"
+
+import atexit
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state as ps
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once
+from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.mp import register_comm_cleanup
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce import (
+    CustomAllreduce,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.srt.utils.cuda_vmm_utils import is_vmm_pointer
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kernels.utils import multigpu_pytest_main
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="extra-b", runner_config="8-gpu-h200")
+
+TEST_SIZES = [16, 1024, 32 * 1024, 1024 * 1024]
+TEST_LAYERS = 4
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _init_groups():
+    local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
+    world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo")
+    ps._WORLD = coord = ps.init_world_group(
+        ranks=list(range(world_size)), local_rank=local_rank, backend="nccl"
+    )
+    get_parallel().override_permanently(world_group=coord)
+    atexit.register(dist.destroy_process_group)
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}")
+    nccl_group = dist.new_group(backend="nccl", device_id=device)
+    return device, coord.cpu_group, nccl_group
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _init_comm() -> CustomAllreduce:
+    device, cpu_group, _ = _init_groups()
+    comm = CustomAllreduce(cpu_group, device)
+    if comm.disabled:
+        # A skip would turn a failing run into "skipped" on hosts without P2P.
+        raise RuntimeError("CustomAllreduce (v1) is disabled on this system")
+    register_comm_cleanup(comm)
+    return comm
+
+
+def test_allocator_is_vmm():
+    device, _, _ = _init_groups()
+    probe = torch.zeros(16, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    assert is_vmm_pointer(probe.data_ptr()), (
+        "expandable_segments is not active; check PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF"
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("from_graph_pool", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("size", TEST_SIZES)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_graph_all_reduce_matches_nccl(size: int, from_graph_pool: bool):
+    device, _, nccl_group = _init_groups()
+    comm = _init_comm()
+    graph_inp = torch.zeros((TEST_LAYERS, size), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    assert is_vmm_pointer(graph_inp.data_ptr())
+    assert not comm.tms_cudagraph
+    assert comm.should_custom_ar(graph_inp[0])
+
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    outs, ptrs = [], []
+    with comm.capture():
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            for i in range(TEST_LAYERS):
+                # In a server the input is an activation from the graph's own
+                # private pool, so cover that source as well.
+                x = graph_inp[i] + 0 if from_graph_pool else graph_inp[i]
+                ptrs.append(x.data_ptr())
+                outs.append(comm.custom_all_reduce(x))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    # Checked after capture so the test makes no driver calls inside it; the
+    # graph keeps these blocks mapped.
+    assert all(is_vmm_pointer(p) for p in ptrs)
+
+    # Small integers stay exact in bf16 after the sum, so compare exactly.
+    inp = torch.randint(0, 16, (TEST_LAYERS, size), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    ref = inp.clone()
+    dist.all_reduce(ref, group=nccl_group)
+    graph_inp.copy_(inp)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(torch.stack(outs), ref, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    multigpu_pytest_main(__name__, __file__, num_gpus=(2,))
